title: Plans to Scram
subtitle: Perfection is his goal, but it remains just that—a goal.

items.text: Plans to Scram
A piece of cloth.
Plain, simple, and smooth.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: You sure this won't fall right off if we wrap it around ourselves?
The followers struggle to arrange the cloth into something resembling a robe.
Clearly, spatial imagination isn't their strong suit.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Ugh! This won't work.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Anyway, their style of dress involves careful folding and binding, not just wrapping like this.
The artist's aesthetic sense kicks in, and with a little work, they begin to look more like numbers.

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: What a hassle.
The followers grumble.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: So, we need to embrace Truth to achieve the soul's … um …

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Oh, my, I never thought I find my own language so difficult.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: You're doing well, but you missed a part, "avoid letting our souls become excessive."

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: Ensure that the soul ... does not indulge in excess.
She stammers through the sentence.

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: Ensure that our souls ... do not indulge ... in excess.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Excellent. Now, say it again.
The not-so-eloquent follower takes a deep breath.

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: Ensure that our souls ... do not indulge in excess.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Very good. Now, our next item is …
Seeing the next item on the list, the artist frowns.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Study math?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Who wrote this?

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: Undercover agents are often exposed due to small oversights.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: As painful as it is, we have to admit that understanding math will be a necessity here.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I admire your courage.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I admire your courage.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Explaining the beauty of mathematics to an irrational number is a challenging task in itself.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: But especially under these circumstances, with the "Emanation" approaching—

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: You shouldn't waste your energy on such trivial matters.
37 turns her face away.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Oh, it's not that they fail to understand the math; they just haven't yet freed themselves from the trivialities of the world of phenomena.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Like the golden spiral. That artist may not know its formula or essence, but that doesn't stop them from using it.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I believe he's learned something from the classes. Hopefully, it brings him closer to the Truth!
Seagulls beyond counting swoop down over the shore.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: Are we supposed to stroll here like their leader does?

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: What's the point of this?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Oh!
He seems a bit disheartened.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I just thought you might appreciate the sunset.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: Sometimes, I feel like we need a translator for your brain.
He turns to his bewildered companion.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: Did you understand what he's going on about?

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: He's ... an artist.

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: But … this path … it feels familiar. I've been here before.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Yeah, everyone should come here to see the sunset.

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: No, I mean ... I have a more important … task.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: Task? You received orders?

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: No, one of ... my own ... ideas.
She points to one side of the beach.

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: I buried ... the bomb ... over there.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: The bomb?

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: Because ... that's where their leader ... is likely to walk …

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: Killing their leader ... would solve our problem ... at the root.

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: Wouldn't it?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Oh, no!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Can you still find the bomb?
In this tense atmosphere, any incident, large or small, could ignite a war.

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: Easier said than ... done.
She raises her hand, pointing to the sand stretching out far beyond sight; all of it indistinguishable.

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: It's somewhere ... out there.
He crouches down, starting his search.
Soon, a shadow looms over him from behind.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Did you find it?

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Are you looking for this?
In the Corrector's hand is a bundle of wires, sensors, and a detonator.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Uh, yes, thank you.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: That is a very dangerous device. Would you give it to me?

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: You're asking me to place a weapon back into the hands of our would-be attacker?
